identity.title: Medium-sized Satellites of Large Kuiper Belt Objects

paper_type_evidence.quote: Using the Atacama Large Millimeter Array, we obtain the first spatially resolved observations of these systems at thermal wavelengths.

question.value: What are the sizes and albedos of Dysnomia (Eris) and Vanth (Orcus), and do they fit the small icy collisional-satellite paradigm?

evidence.quote: We calculate a diameter for Dysnomia of 700$\pm$115 km and for Vanth of 475$\pm$75 km, with albedos of 0.04$^{+0.02}_{-0.01}$ and 0.08$\pm$0.02 respectively.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00830.S, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.00810.S.

findings_qualitative.value: Neither Vanth nor Dysnomia fits the small icy collisional satellite paradigm; both have low albedos typical of KBOs their size

evidence.quote: Indeed, both Dysnomia and Vanth have the low albedos expected for typical KBOs of their size

claims.hypothesis: Are Dysnomia and Vanth small, high-albedo icy collisional fragments?
claims.experiment: Resolved ALMA Band 7 thermal flux plus thermal-model MCMC
claims.result: Dysnomia 700±115 km, albedo 0.04; Vanth 475±75 km, albedo 0.08
claims.finding: Both are indistinguishable from typical KBOs of their size, not icy fragments

evidence.quote: Both Dysnomia and Vanth are indistinguishable from typical Kuiper belt objects of their size.
